question: Can a preregistered trust radius on function-fitted shear coordinates retain the stable weight/post-GELU geometry of task-selected shear while preserving its observed MLP-output and CE-gradient gain?

fixed_protocol.topology: unchanged task/weight-selected shear24 topology after the qualified fresh64 rotational parent
fixed_protocol.fit: fit function-space shear coordinates once at radius 1.0 on the registered fit window, then replay exact determinant-one maps after multiplying only those coordinates by each registered radius
fixed_protocol.scoring: exact nonlinear GELU and fixed-c_proj MLP-output effects, weight recovery, and predicted CE descent on fit plus a new independent train holdout

decision_rule.selection: A radius passes only if the same preregistered radius beats weight-shear24 MLP-output recovery by at least 1.10x on both fit and new holdout, retains at least 0.90x post-GELU and weight recovery, does not reduce predicted CE descent on either window, and passes finite-map conditioning. If multiple radii pass, select the smallest. No threshold changes after observation.

limitations: This is a zero-update structural diagnostic; no validation CE, parameter update, optimizer update, or training is performed.
The fit window and radius-1 ablation were observed in the parent diagnostic. The holdout train seed is new and scoring-only; the complete radius grid and gates are frozen before reading it.

This is not the rejected 2026-08-01 fresh88 trust-radius experiment. That experiment scaled the complete finite Muon update. This experiment keeps the rotational parent and weight-selected topology fixed and scales only newly function-fitted shear coordinates.
Passing authorizes only a separately preregistered finite-CE gate. It does not authorize production integration, MFU testing, scientific training, or a larger rung.
